hints: Flip the question: instead of choosing what to cancel, how many shows can you KEEP? Which show is the safest one to keep first?
Greedy by end time: sort shows by end, keep a show whenever it starts at or after the end of the last kept show. Cancelled = total − kept.

1. Sort shows by end time.
  2. Set lastEnd = −infinity, kept = 0.
  3. For each show: if start ≥ lastEnd, keep it (kept++, lastEnd = its end).
  4. Return n − kept.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every subset of shows, check if it is clash-free, and take the largest one.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Sort by start and do a DP: best[i] = max kept shows ending with show i.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Sort by end time and greedily keep each show that starts after the last kept one ends.

explain: Sample 1 sorted by end: [1,3],[2,4],[1,5],[3,5]. Keep [1,3] (lastEnd = 3); [2,4] starts at 2 < 3 → cancel; [1,5] → cancel; [3,5] starts at 3 ≥ 3 → keep. Kept 2 of 4, so cancel 2. The show that finishes earliest leaves the most room for everything after it, so choosing it never hurts — that is the exchange argument. Note that touching shows (start == previous end) do not clash, so the check is ≥.
recognize: Remove the fewest intervals so the rest don't overlap → keep the maximum set of non-overlapping intervals by earliest end.
